source_document: Gettysburg Total War animation plan, version 2, B.9.1 Tables 1-5, pdf pages 103-110; text docs/battle-theatre/BIBLE/plan-clean.txt lines 24884-26350
transcription_rules: Cell text as printed, straight quotes, line breaks joined. URLs exactly as printed (including ones the PDF shows truncated). Null = column not printed in that table. check_* fields are observations by the task that built this file, not PDF content.
law: Nothing here is verified by being listed. A source gives a documented basis only for what it states (PDF B.9). Tiers R1-R4 describe use as a 1863 landscape source, not archive quality.

tier_definitions.R1: Measured survey or measured geodata. Positional accuracy can be tested.
tier_definitions.R2: Near-contemporary map, photograph or record (1858 to about 1876) made by or near the people who saw the ground.
tier_definitions.R3: Later, derived or secondary product (restoration GIS, books, summaries, Wikipedia-level pages). Useful, but must be cross-checked.
tier_definitions.R4: Artistic or composite work, or a forum or blog claim. Low weight. Never the sole basis for any object.

method_limits: The research passes had several blocked endpoints: loc.gov search and JSON endpoints were blocked to the research tools, several Rumsey and NARA catalog pages returned verification screens, and the NPS Little Round Top cultural landscape report PDF failed to fetch. Items that depend on those pages are marked "URL unverified". Claude Code retries these during execution (Part D, Part E); the retry results go into the Evidence-Gap Register. Nothing below is presented as verified when the notes say it was not. (PDF B.9, page 104)

rows.name: NPS park GIS 1863 layers (Curtis Musselman, park GIS)
rows.type: Vector GIS of historic roads, lanes, fence lines, property boundaries and buildings "as they stood in 1863", with 1895, 1927 and 1993 periods
rows.what_it_gives: Georeferencing method: the LOC 1886 tracing scanned at 300 dpi (a 72 dpi NARA copy was too blurry); affine registration on nine control points (building corners, fence intersections), then rubbersheeting; large-scale features (woods, fields, orchards, roads) and small-scale features (fences, lanes, trees) digitized

rows.limits: No public download of the 1863 layers was found; they appear to be request-only. Claude Code therefore re-creates the same layers itself from the Warren IIIF (B.9.2) and uses a request to the NPS GIS office as a parallel route, recorded in the register as "request not answered" if no reply comes.
pdf_unverified_flags: PDF: no public download found; layers appear request-only; licence unknown.
check_notes: check_14: a request to the NPS GIS office is a message sent on the owner's behalf; per CLAUDE.md it is an owner-only act (sending permission requests).

rows.table_title: Table 2. Park GIS, reconstructions and restoration studies
rows.name: Knowles et al. 2013 reconstruction (Anne Kelly Knowles lead; Dan Miller, Alex Tait for 1863 terrain; Allen Carroll; Tim Montenyohl; Judith Nielsen)
rows.what_it_gives: Digitization precedent and the only published error statement. Knowles hand-traced 4-ft contours from a 1:12,000 engraved Warren-derived map (about 1874; survey by Lt. William H. Chase under Warren), built a TIN and georectified on buildings unchanged since 1863. Hilltops and ridgelines differ from the 1996 DEM by under 50 ft; creek beds and rolling ground by much more (hundreds of feet in places per the second note). The notes phrase the 50 ft figure both as elevation difference and as displacement; the pipeline treats both as unresolved and measures its own.
rows.limits: The data are not stated as downloadable. Knowles' team did not build a vegetation dataset. Author most confident about areas Lee could not see. Tested the Codori-Trostle thicket height in viewsheds.
pdf_unverified_flags: PDF: the 50 ft figure is stated both as elevation difference and as displacement; unresolved (pipeline measures its own).
PDF: data not stated as downloadable.
check_notes: check_15: the PDF dates the Knowles base map "about 1874, survey by Lt. William H. Chase under Warren" while the project's LOC read says the Warren sheet was surveyed 1868-69 and revised on the ground 1873 by P. M. Blake (docs/basemap1863/SOURCES-landcover.md). Row 2 of the PDF also says "1868-69, revised 1873". The two attributions are not reconciled in the PDF; verify before citing either name.
rows.transcription_note: The PDF breaks several URLs at hyphens; joined without spaces. The row text continues onto page 106.

rows.name: PHMC agricultural census extracts
rows.what_it_gives: County agricultural census extracts for 1850, 1880, 1927 (path pattern phmc.pa.gov/Preservation/<year>-Agricultural-Census/Documents/adams_county_<year>_census_data.pdf)

check_notes: check_41: the extracts listed are 1850, 1880 and 1927. B.9.2 step 5 says "the 1860 agricultural census and the damage claims (Table 4, rows 39 and 41)" would convert inference to documented fact; row 41 contains no 1860 extract. The 1860 census is therefore not in the catalog; B.9.3 routes it to NARA, FamilySearch or Ancestry, two of which need accounts (CLAUDE.md: no accounts by Claude: owner-only).

rows.name: NPS natural features and ecosystems
rows.what_it_gives: Park of 5,989 acres; more than 1,600 acres woodlot/forest; more than 2,300 acres crop/pasture/meadow; about 148 acres palustrine wetland; forest regeneration study since 1985; 1999 General Management Plan/EIS aims to replant historic woodlots, orchards and thickets
rows.limits: Modern.

rows.name: NPS plants
rows.what_it_gives: Modern woodlot overstory dominated by white oak, white ash, northern red oak; 553 vascular plants (410 native); invasives include ailanthus and multiflora rose; no mention of American chestnut
rows.limits: Modern species list under-represents 1863 composition (see B.10.3).

rows.name: American Battlefield Trust, battlefield orchards
rows.what_it_gives: 44 orchards existed on present park land during the war; since 2000 NPS planted 2,869 apple trees on 109 acres at 35 historic orchard sites; the Sherfy Peach Orchard was replanted in 2008 with 72 peach trees; 114 Sherfy trees survived the battle
rows.limits: The notes elsewhere say the Sherfy orchard was replanted in 1883 and that Gilbert Orchard was replanted in 2007; replanted extent exceeds the 1863 extent. 1863 species are unknown.
pdf_unverified_flags: PDF: internal conflict on replanting dates (2008 / 1883 for Sherfy; Gilbert 2007).
check_notes: check_44: conflicting replanting dates are carried in the PDF itself ("2008" in this row versus "1883" elsewhere in its notes); keep as a conflict-register entry rather than choosing.
rows.transcription_note: The PDF breaks the URL after "hidden-"; joined without a space.

rows.name: Fence evidence
rows.what_it_gives: Post-and-rail (posts in dug holes) and Virginia worm/sawbuck (zig-zag rails, no post holes, possibly used where ground was rocky) described along the Emmitsburg Road; post and rail lined both sides and Pickett's attackers crossed two fences. General post-and-rail dimensions (not Gettysburg-specific): rails about 11 ft, height about 5 ft, posts 6 to 6.5 ft; oak/locust/cedar posts, oak/poplar/pine rails
rows.limits: Blog-level sources. No documented list of stone walls versus rail fences by location. Feeds B.8.
pdf_unverified_flags: PDF: blog-level sources only.
rows.transcription_note: The PDF breaks URLs at hyphens; joined without spaces.
